direction: Explore new priority rules for the CVRP greedy construction.

operations.mechanism: Try a different combination of distance, depot distance and load.

preserve: The problem interface, the evaluator and the search policy.
hypothesis: A different distance/load combination yields better routes.

research_activity.question: Are the priority scores this search writes invariant to the numerical scale at which the same instance is expressed?
research_activity.finding_summary: The near-tie gate of the previous batch is not invariant to coordinate scale: re-expressing them at 1e-2 and 1e-3 of nominal size raises the share of steps entering the gate from 1.3% to 64% and 83%, and degrades the scale-normalised objective from 10.92 to 16.20 and 33.52 (+48%, +207%). At nominal scale it fires on only 1.3% of steps, so it is nearly dead there. The width adds an absolute length to a relative term. Keeping only the relative part removes the scale dependence (spread 0.39% over four scales) but gives back 1.92% at nominal, so invariance alone is not a win: the nominal regression has to stay near zero too. A rule that only replaces the width therefore loses at nominal scale; the trade-off, not either half alone, is the payment.
